questions.q: What is the core distinction between the Qiskit SDK and the IBM Quantum Platform?
options: They are two names for the exact same product
The SDK is a paid desktop application; the Platform is free
The SDK is a free, local, open-source Python library; the Platform is IBM's account-gated cloud service providing real hardware access
The SDK only works on Windows; the Platform is cross-platform
questions.explain: The Qiskit SDK runs entirely on your own machine with no account needed. The IBM Quantum Platform is a separate cloud service requiring an account, used to reach real quantum hardware.

questions.q: Why can you build and debug circuits through most of this course entirely offline?
options: Because `AerSimulator` is a classical, local simulation requiring no account or network call
Because the IBM Quantum Platform has no usage limits
Because offline mode automatically caches real hardware results from previous users
Because Qiskit disables internet access by default for security
questions.explain: `AerSimulator` runs classically on your own CPU. It needs no account, no internet connection, and no Platform access, which is exactly why it's the right place to build and debug circuits before they ever touch real hardware.

questions.q: What does the IBM Quantum Platform give you that local simulation with `AerSimulator` fundamentally cannot?
options: Faster circuit construction syntax
A measurement from an actual physical quantum device, with real hardware noise and constraints
The ability to use `QuantumCircuit`
Free unlimited compute with no quotas of any kind
questions.explain: Local simulation reproduces the logic and expected statistics of a circuit, but it cannot give you a result from a real physical device. That's the one thing only the Platform's hardware access provides.

questions.q: According to the lesson, how should you treat any specific number you read about IBM's free-tier usage quota?
options: As a permanently fixed number you should memorize now
As irrelevant, since the free tier never has any limits
As something that may be out of date — verify current numbers on IBM's own pricing/plans page when it actually matters
As a number that only applies to paid accounts, not free ones
questions.explain: IBM periodically adjusts free-tier quotas. The lesson explicitly advises checking current official documentation rather than trusting a memorized or previously-read figure.

questions.q: When does this course say you'll actually need to work directly with the IBM Quantum Platform?
options: Immediately, before writing your first circuit
Never — the whole course stays on the local simulator
Starting in Chapter 5, once circuit-construction and simulation fundamentals are already built
Only if you fail the Chapter 1 quiz
questions.explain: The course front-loads circuit-building and local simulation skills and only brings the Platform into direct use starting in Chapter 5, once those fundamentals are in place.
